docs.title: Bharat Agentic Commerce Protocol
docs.text:
BACP lets an AI agent discover, negotiate, buy, pay for, return and raise grievances about goods and services in India, on behalf of a person or a business, within limits that person or business has signed.

Version 2026-10-18

BACP 2026-10-18 is the first dated release of the specification, and implementers can target it. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release. The conformance test suite is not yet published, so no participant can hold a conformance attestation yet. BACP is an independent proposal: it is not issued or endorsed by NPCI, ONDC, RBI or any other public body. Send feedback on GitHub.

Read the specification Core concepts View on GitHub

docs.title: Why BACP
docs.text:
India already has the rails that agentic commerce needs. ONDC and Beckn provide an open commerce network with order, cancel, return and grievance flows. UPI moves money at population scale and already has standing-authority primitives such as UPI Circle, Reserve Pay and AutoPay. Account Aggregator consent shows how to make permission explicit, purpose-bound and revocable. The DPDP Act sets the rules for personal data.

As of 17-10-2026, none of these rails has a published, standard way to identify agents. A network message identifies the buyer app, not the agent that acted. A payment carries no record of what the user allowed the agent to do. Nothing standard says whether a human was present, how a user revokes an agent, or how a dispute can reconstruct what the agent was told.

Global agentic-commerce protocols solve parts of this problem, but, as of 17-10-2026, they are built mainly around cards and around single merchants. None of them defines how to use UPI, cash on delivery, GST, Indian-language voice or the ONDC network.

BACP is a thin agent layer over the Indian rails. It replaces none of them. It adds four things to every transaction:

  • who the agent is, as a signed and registered credential;
  • on whose authority it acts, and within what limits, as a signed mandate;
  • whether a human was present when it acted;
  • what the user agreed to share, as a DPDP consent receipt.

Every step leaves verifiable evidence, so that a dispute can be traced from the user's instruction to the UPI reference number.

docs.title: What the first release covers
docs.text: BACP 2026-10-18 leads with marketplace and quick commerce (b2c.ecom), and launches with kirana khata, subscriptions and ticketing. These four trade profiles are stable. Distributor schemes and B2B procurement, services and social commerce are in the release as proposed profiles: attestable, but their rules MAY change in a later dated release. GeM, agri and mandi trade, cross-border trade, high-value purchases, rentals and assisted rural commerce are in review: described so that readers can comment, outside the conformance scope of this release, and open to change or removal. Trade profiles lists the maturity of each.

docs.title: Who it is for
docs.text: You are What BACP gives you An agent builder One way to discover, check out, negotiate, pay and raise grievances across the ONDC network, over REST, MCP or A2A, without a separate integration for each seller. A buyer app (BAP) A gateway model for hosting agents safely: a deterministic mandate verifier, signed agent requests, and idempotency and replay protection on top of Beckn. A seller or seller app (BPP) Agent orders you can trust: a declared and signed agent, a mandate reference, a hash of the cart the user approved, and structured negotiation that never leaks the buyer's walk-away price. A PSP, bank or issuer A clean binding between an agent mandate and the UPI and other Indian payment primitives you already run, with a basket-blind payment leg and signed receipts. A regulator or policy team A concrete, reviewable proposal for how agent commerce can meet RBI authentication rules, DPDP consent, e-commerce consumer protection and grievance timelines.

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
• Mandate-bound agents

    An agent acts only under a signed mandate, open or closed, with budgets, allow-lists, step-up thresholds and fast revocation. The agent is never an authentication factor.

    Mandates and consent →

  • Native UPI and all Indian rails

    Open mandates bind to UPI Circle, Reserve Pay, AutoPay and One-Time Mandate. (As of 17-10-2026, NPCI lists AI-driven payments through UPI Circle as a closed-user-group pilot.) A registry of payment handlers covers cards, net banking, wallets, BBPS, e-RUPI, NACH, cash on delivery and B2B credit.

    Payments →

  • Built on ONDC/Beckn

    BACP rides on Beckn's search, select, init, confirm, cancel, update and IGM flows. Agent data travels in a namespaced extension that existing network participants can ignore.

    Beckn / ONDC binding →

  • Negotiation the way India trades

    Mol-bhav, B2B price rounds, RFQs, reverse auctions and schemes. The language model proposes and a deterministic guard decides. The reservation price never leaves the buyer's side.

    Negotiation →

  • DPDP-grade consent

    Mandates follow Account Aggregator consent semantics: immutable, purpose-bound, use-counted and revocable. Every data share produces a consent receipt in the user's language.

    Security and privacy →

  • Verifiable evidence and IGM

    A hash-chained instruction log and rail-anchored receipts link the prompt, intent, cart, mandate and UPI RRN. Agents raise grievances through ONDC IGM with that evidence attached.

    Evidence →

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    U["User"] -->|"approves mandate on the Trusted Surface"| MM["Mandate Manager"]
    A["Agent"] -->|"signed request with mandate"| G["BACP gateway<br/>in a buyer app"]
    MM -.->|"mandate status"| G
    G -->|"Beckn with context.bacp"| S["Seller apps on ONDC"]
    G -->|"basket-blind payment leg"| P["Payer PSP and UPI"]
    P -->|"signed receipt with RRN"| G
    G -->|"instruction log and receipts"| E["Evidence bundle"]

Core concepts explains each part. BACP and India's DPI explains what BACP takes from each rail, and BACP and other protocols explains how it relates to UCP, AP2, ACP, A2A and MCP.

docs.title: An independent, open proposal
docs.text:
BACP is an independent open proposal. It is not issued, endorsed or operated by NPCI, ONDC, RBI or any other public body. As of 17-10-2026, no production deployments have been announced. Where it relies on a rail or a regulation, it describes that rail as publicly documented and leaves the rail's own rules in charge.

The specification, schemas and tools are developed in the open at github.com/bacp-dev/bacp under the Apache License 2.0. See Status and Roadmap for what comes next.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
This page describes how the BACP specification is versioned, released and maintained: the version identifiers, the URLs under which each version is published, how schema identifiers resolve, what counts as a breaking change, and when fixes are backported to a published release.

Version 2026-10-18

The current dated release is 2026-10-18, the first dated release of BACP. Where this page says "approved", the approval is given by the release approvers defined in GOVERNANCE.md, following the process on this page.

docs.title: Version identifiers
docs.text:
BACP versions are calendar dates in the form YYYY-MM-DD, for example 2026-10-18. The date is the day the release is cut. Dates give a clear chronological order and make versions easy to compare. Version identifiers use YYYY-MM-DD so that they sort correctly in URLs, tags and schema ids; dates elsewhere in the documentation are shown as DD-MM-YYYY.

  • draft is the working version on the main branch. It has no date and may change at any time, including in breaking ways.
  • A dated release D is a snapshot of the whole protocol, published and tested together as one compatible set:
    • the specification pages;
    • the JSON Schemas;
    • the OpenAPI document of the REST binding;
    • the payment handler registry and the conformance manifest.

The first dated release is 2026-10-18. draft remains the working version built from main, where changes for later releases are made.

A verifier chooses the rules to apply to a mandate by the dated release that the mandate names (for a Payment Mandate, the rail_binding.registry_version of the open Payment Mandate it is or narrows; a Checkout Mandate names none, and the verifier applies the release in force at its iat), never by its vct. The vct names a mandate type, such as in.bacp.mandate.payment.open.1, and does not change when a release adds a field or a rule.

A participant states the version it speaks in its gateway profile (bacp.version and bacp.supported_versions at /.well-known/bacp), and the gateway states it on the network leg in context.bacp.version. See Discovery and Profiles.

docs.title: Published URLs
docs.text:
The specification is published at bacp.dev with one directory per version.

URL Contents https://bacp.dev/ This site: the overview pages, which are not versioned https://bacp.dev/draft/ The specification built from main. Unstable. https://bacp.dev/YYYY-MM-DD/ The specification of the dated release YYYY-MM-DD. Stable, amended only by approved backports. https://bacp.dev/latest/ An alias of the newest dated release. It points at 2026-10-18.

Links from the overview pages into the specification go to /latest/. To cite a rule that must not move, link to a dated release.

docs.title: Schema identifiers
docs.text:
Every BACP JSON Schema has an $id under https://bacp.dev/schemas/, for example https://bacp.dev/schemas/mandate.json. When a version is published, each schema is written to the path named by its $id within that version's directory, and its $id and every https://bacp.dev/schemas/… $ref are rewritten to the versioned form. The OpenAPI document is rewritten the same way.

Identifier Resolves to Use it when https://bacp.dev/schemas/<name>.json The schema in the latest release You want whatever is current, for example in documentation https://bacp.dev/YYYY-MM-DD/schemas/<name>.json The schema pinned to release YYYY-MM-DD You validate production traffic or artefacts: always pin https://bacp.dev/draft/schemas/<name>.json The schema on main You track unreleased work

Because published schemas reference each other by versioned $id, a schema fetched from a dated release always resolves its $refs within the same release. Tools MUST resolve $refs by $id, not by local file path.

Signed artefacts (mandates, receipts, credentials) are long-lived evidence. Verifiers SHOULD validate them against the schemas of the version under which they were issued.

docs.title: Release branches
docs.text:
New work happens on main, which is published as draft.

  • When a release is approved, a branch named release/YYYY-MM-DD is cut from main. The release branch is frozen from that moment: only changes allowed by the backport policy may land on it.
  • A change found to be needed after the branch is cut is made in one of two ways:
    1. on the release branch, then merged to main; or
    2. on main, then cherry-picked to the release branch.
  • Once final, the release is tagged vYYYY-MM-DD and published at https://bacp.dev/YYYY-MM-DD/, and latest moves to it.
  • Release branches are long-lived. Each one is kept for reference and maintenance of its published version.

docs.title: Backwards-compatible changes
docs.text:
These changes do not break a conforming participant and MAY be made within a release line by backport:

  • adding an optional field to a response, webhook or network message (receivers ignore unknown fields);
  • adding an optional request parameter;
  • adding a new endpoint, operation or webhook type;
  • registering a new error or message code with an existing HTTP status class and resolution;
  • adding a value to an enumeration that is not documented as exhaustive;
  • adding a payment handler descriptor, or a new alias for an existing handler;
  • clarifying text without changing behaviour.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text:
These changes break conforming participants and MUST go into a new dated release:

  • removing or renaming a field, endpoint, operation, webhook or header;
  • changing a field's type or meaning;
  • making an optional field required;
  • changing a state machine or the order of a protocol flow;
  • changing authentication, signature coverage, signature tags or replay rules;
  • changing the meaning, HTTP status or resolution of an existing error code;
  • adding a new mandate constraint key. Verifiers fail closed on unknown constraints, so a new constraint would make older verifiers reject every mandate that uses it. New families of bounds go into a new mandate type instead;
  • tightening a validation rule so that previously valid artefacts fail;
  • removing a handler alias at the end of its deprecation window.

docs.title: Deprecation
docs.text:
A field, code or handler alias that will be removed is first marked deprecated in a release, and removed in a later release. Handler aliases from earlier naming schemes are accepted for one deprecation window.

As policy of this release, a deprecated field, code or handler alias stays supported for at least two dated releases after the release that deprecates it, and for at least 180 days after that release, whichever is later. It may be removed only in a dated release after both periods have passed. (This settles the deprecation window asked about in Q-28.)

docs.title: Breaking-change policy
docs.text:
• A breaking change MUST be marked as breaking in its change request (for example with ! in the pull-request title) and MUST be listed in the release notes of the release that introduces it.
  • A breaking change MUST be announced publicly before it is merged. As policy of this release, a breaking change gets at least 90 days' notice in the release notes before the dated release that introduces it is published.
  • Security-sensitive fixes are the exception: their disclosure timeline is set case by case, so a fix is not announced before it is safe to disclose.
  • draft on main is unstable: work towards a later release lands there first and may change before it is released. The notice period applies to the dated release that ships a breaking change, not to each change on main.

docs.title: Backport policy
docs.text:
• An approved backwards-compatible change (a security, correctness or interoperability fix, or a small addition) MAY be backported to a supported dated release. The release keeps its date, and its published artefacts are amended in place.
  • A breaking change is not backported by default. In exceptional cases a breaking change MAY be backported when the release as published compromises security, correctness or interoperability, following the breaking-change notice process.
  • Before amended artefacts are published, the release's conformance suite MUST pass again against the amended release.
  • Because a dated release can be amended, parties that fetch its artefacts at run time SHOULD follow standard HTTP caching and revalidate cached copies when they expire. A copy fetched earlier is missing later additions but, because backports are backwards-compatible by default, does not conflict with them.

docs.title: Registry release manifest
docs.text:
The handler registry and the conformance-authority list are data, and a backport can amend them in place under the same date. So every publication of these files carries a release manifest, source/handlers/release.json, valid against registry-release.json:

  • registry_version is the dated release (YYYY-MM-DD).
  • registry_serial is an integer of at least 1 that strictly increases across every publication, including every backport to a dated release, so that two publications of the same registry_version are ordered. A mandate pause lifts only on a greater serial (Handler binding).
  • published_at is an RFC 3339 timestamp in IST (+05:30). The 24-hour freshness rule of a gateway runs from it.
  • files[] lists each file's uri (a URI reference resolved against the manifest) and its digest: sha-256: and the unpadded base64url SHA-256 over the file's RFC 8785 (JCS) form. A byte hash would not match the served file, because the site build re-serialises each JSON file.

There is no registry-signed snapshot. No party holds a registry signing key, so the dated release and its manifest are the only source of the registry. A signed snapshot MAY be added later, once a holder of a registry key exists, without a breaking change.

docs.title: Core Concepts
docs.text:
This page explains the main ideas in BACP in plain terms. The specification gives the normative rules. Where this page and the specification differ, the specification wins.

Version 2026-10-18

This page describes BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed in the specification depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release. They are listed on the open questions page.

docs.title: The idea in one paragraph
docs.text: An AI agent that shops for someone in India needs to do four things the existing rails do not support: prove who it is, prove what it is allowed to do, show whether its principal was present, and show what personal data the principal agreed to share. BACP adds these four things as signed artefacts that travel with ordinary ONDC/Beckn messages and ordinary UPI payments. The rails stay in charge of what they already do. BACP adds the agent layer and the evidence.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text:
BACP is built in layers. Each layer reuses an existing standard or rail where one exists.

flowchart TB
    T["Transport bindings<br/>REST, MCP, A2A"]
    F["BACP session facade<br/>checkout, negotiation, post-order, evidence"]
    B["ONDC / Beckn network<br/>search, select, init, confirm, cancel, update, IGM"]
    R["Payment rails<br/>UPI and other Indian rails"]
    C["Consent<br/>mandates and consent receipts"]
    I["Identity<br/>agent credentials and request signatures"]
    T --> F
    F --> B
    F --> R
    C -.-> F
    I -.-> T

Solid arrows are calls. Dotted arrows are trust dependencies: every call is checked against a mandate and a signed agent identity.

docs.title: Actors
docs.text:
Actor Role in BACP User (principal) The person or business the agent acts for. Approves mandates, answers step-ups and enters the UPI PIN or other authentication factor. Can pause or revoke a mandate at any time. Agent The AI runtime, text or voice. It finds products, builds carts, negotiates and asks for payment. BACP treats it as untrusted: it never holds a PIN or OTP, never signs consent and is never an authentication factor. Agent operator The legal entity that operates the agent. It holds the agent's credential, keeps the signing key out of the agent's reach, discloses that the user is dealing with an AI, and offers a human handoff. Buyer app (BAP) with a BACP gateway The registered ONDC buyer app that hosts the gateway. It verifies agent signatures and mandates in deterministic code, talks Beckn to the network and keeps the evidence. Seller app (BPP) and seller Publish catalogues, quote, fulfil, handle cancellations and returns, issue GST invoices and respond to grievances. Mandate Manager Turns the user's approval into a signed mandate and consent receipt, tracks use and revocation, and publishes status. It does not see order or payment payloads. Trusted Surface A non-agentic screen, usually the user's UPI or banking app, where the user reviews and approves a mandate and authenticates. Payer PSP, issuer and NPCI Execute the payment and enforce rail limits. In BACP the payer PSP also returns a signed receipt with the UPI RRN. They see the payee and amount, not the basket.

See the glossary for the full list of terms.

docs.title: Mandates
docs.text:
A mandate is a signed, immutable statement of what an agent may do for its principal. It is the centre of BACP. Every action the gateway takes is checked against one.

BACP's mandates are wire-compatible with the open and closed mandates of the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), and follow the consent-artefact model of Account Aggregator.

  • An open mandate sets constraints for future actions when the user will not be present: a budget per day, week or month, allowed categories, sellers and delivery PIN codes, a step-up threshold, and an expiry.
  • A closed mandate approves one exact cart or one exact payment.
  • A Checkout Mandate authorises what may be bought. A Payment Mandate authorises how it may be paid. A separate negotiation mandate holds bargaining bounds, including the walk-away price, which never leaves the buyer's side.
  • Each mandate records whether the human was present (HP) or not present (HNP).
  • A mandate can be paused, revoked or exhausted. Revocation reaches the gateway quickly, and the gateway stops all in-flight sessions under that mandate.
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant TS as Trusted Surface
    participant MM as Mandate Manager
    participant A as Agent
    participant G as BACP gateway
    U->>TS: Approve "groceries, up to ₹3,000 a month"
    TS->>MM: Approval with UPI PIN
    MM-->>A: Signed open mandate
    A->>G: Cart of ₹850 with mandate reference
    G->>G: Verify budget, category, PIN code, step-up rule
    G-->>A: Within mandate, proceed
    A->>G: Cart of ₹2,400
    G-->>A: Above step-up threshold, ask the user

Read more: Mandates and Consent.

docs.title: The gateway: an agent layer over Beckn
docs.text:
ONDC and Beckn are asynchronous. A buyer app sends search or select and receives on_search or on_select later, from many sellers. Agents work better with a synchronous session that always returns the full, authoritative state.

The BACP gateway provides that. It runs inside, or on behalf of, a registered buyer app and:

  • exposes checkout sessions with familiar verbs (create, update, complete, cancel) and full-state responses;
  • turns each call into the matching Beckn messages, carrying agent data in a namespaced context.bacp extension that existing network participants can ignore;
  • verifies the agent's signature, credential and mandate before anything leaves the gateway;
  • adds what Beckn leaves optional: mandatory idempotency keys, a replay cache, and request signatures bound to callbacks;
  • records every step in the instruction log.
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Agent
    participant G as BACP gateway
    participant BG as Beckn gateway
    participant S as Seller app
    A->>G: Create checkout session
    G->>BG: search with context.bacp
    BG->>S: search
    S-->>G: on_search
    G->>S: select
    S-->>G: on_select with signed quote
    G-->>A: Session with full state and quote

The gateway does not change Beckn. A seller app that does not understand BACP can still serve an agent order, because the core Beckn messages are unchanged. Read more: Sessions and Checkout and Beckn / ONDC Binding.

docs.title: Payment handlers
docs.text:
India has many ways to pay, and they have very different rules about when a human must be present. BACP describes each one as a payment handler: a data record that states the rail, the regulator, the limits, the authentication model, the refund route and the settlement evidence. Limits are configuration, not code.

Handlers fall into binding classes:

Class Meaning Examples O (open-eligible) A standing authority whose limits the rail enforces. May back an open mandate, so the agent can pay without the user present. UPI Reserve Pay, UPI Circle, UPI AutoPay, UPI One-Time Mandate, card e-mandate, NACH, e-RUPI C (closed) Needs the user's own authentication for this one payment. UPI intent and QR, cards, net banking, BNPL, 123PAY A (assisted or device-bound) Only on the payer's own device or at an assisted counter. Never usable by a remote agent. UPI Lite, card present, UPI Tap & Pay D (deferred) The order can be placed now, and payment happens later with a human. Cash on delivery, pay on delivery by UPI N (non-paying) Financing, verification or tracking only. TReDS, letter of credit, GeM payment tracking

The agent never sees a PIN, OTP, card number or bank credential. The payment leg sent to the PSP carries only the payee, amount, mandate reference and a hash of the checkout, so the payment rail stays basket-blind.

Read more: Payments, Handler Registry and Rail Bindings.

docs.title: Negotiation
docs.text:
Much of Indian trade is negotiated: mol-bhav in a market, price rounds with a distributor, an RFQ to several suppliers, a reverse auction for a public buyer. BACP supports these as declared modes: fixed price, posted dynamic price, alternating offers, sealed and iterated RFQs, English, reverse-L1 and Dutch auctions, and scheme claims such as bank offers and slab discounts.

Three rules make agent negotiation safe:

  1. Only structured, signed and expiring messages bind. Chat, voice and model explanations are advisory and are logged, but they never form a contract.
  2. The language model proposes and a deterministic guard decides. Every firm counter, acceptance or bid is checked against the negotiation mandate outside the model. The model sees only a verdict: acceptable, not acceptable, or needs escalation.
  3. The reservation price never leaves the buyer's side. The seller sees only a signed attestation that the deal is within bounds.

Silence is never acceptance: a negotiation that gets no reply expires. Indian commercial rules such as MRP ceilings and the MSMED payment-days limit are checked as validators, not left as guidance.

sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Buyer agent
    participant G as Guard in gateway
    participant S as Seller
    S->>A: Offer ₹1,450, valid 10 minutes
    A->>G: Draft counter ₹1,200
    G-->>A: Acceptable
    G->>S: Signed counter ₹1,200
    S->>A: Counter ₹1,320
    A->>G: Draft accept ₹1,320
    G-->>A: Needs escalation
    A->>A: Ask the principal on the Trusted Surface

Read more: Negotiation and RFQ and Auctions.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
When an agent makes a mistake, someone has to work out what happened. BACP makes that possible by design.

  • The instruction log is a hash-chained record of each stage: the user's prompt, the agent's interpreted intent, the cart, the mandate checks, the step-ups and the payment.
  • Receipts are signed by the party that acted. A payment receipt is signed by the PSP and carries the UPI RRN and UTR, or the equivalent reference for other rails.
  • An evidence bundle joins these together. An agent can attach it when it raises a grievance through ONDC's Issue and Grievance Management (IGM) flow, and it can be joined to the RRN for a UPI dispute.
flowchart LR
    P["Prompt"] --> I["Intent"] --> C["Cart and quote"] --> M["Mandate check"] --> Y["Payment receipt with RRN"]
    P -.-> L["Hash-chained instruction log"]
    I -.-> L
    C -.-> L
    M -.-> L
    Y -.-> L
    L --> B["Evidence bundle for IGM or UPI dispute"]

BACP does not decide who is liable when an agent errs within a valid mandate. It makes the evidence complete so that the parties, the networks and the regulators can decide. Read more: Evidence and Instruction Log.

docs.title: Identity and signing
docs.text:
Every agent carries an agent credential bound to its operator's legal entity and to the buyer app that hosts it. Every agent request is signed with HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421), with separate signature tags for browsing, paying and post-order actions. On the network leg, the buyer app still signs Beckn messages with its registry key as usual.

Read more: Identity and Request Signing.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Getting Started walks through a first integration.
  • BACP and India's DPI explains how BACP uses each Indian rail.
  • BACP and other protocols compares BACP with UCP, AP2, ACP and others.

docs.title: BACP and India's DPI
docs.text:
BACP is designed to sit on top of India's digital public infrastructure (DPI), not beside it. This page explains, rail by rail, what BACP uses, what it adds for agents, and what it deliberately leaves to the rail.

The rule throughout is simple: the rail is authoritative. If a UPI limit, an ONDC policy or a regulation says no, the answer is no. BACP re-checks the same limits in the gateway so that it can fail early and fail closed, and it records the evidence, but it never overrides the rail.

Independent proposal

BACP is an independent open proposal. It is not issued or endorsed by NPCI, ONDC, RBI, MeitY or any other body named on this page. Descriptions of each rail are based on public documents. Where a public source is unclear or conflicting, the specification says so and links the open questions.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Infrastructure What BACP uses What BACP adds What BACP leaves to the rail ONDC / Beckn The transaction grammar, registry and signing, post-order flows, IGM Agent identity, mandate references and presence in context.bacp; a synchronous session facade; mandatory idempotency and replay protection Network membership, seller onboarding, catalogue rules, settlement, network policy UPI Circle, Reserve Pay, AutoPay, One-Time Mandate, intent and QR, refunds, disputes A binding from an open mandate to a live UPI primitive; a basket-blind payment leg; signed receipts with the RRN Authentication, limits, debit execution, refunds, chargebacks, UDIR Account Aggregator / DEPA The consent-artefact model Mandates with the same semantics, applied to commerce actions instead of data fetches Financial data sharing itself DPDP Act Notice, consent, withdrawal, Consent Manager rules Consent receipts per recipient, purpose-bound data scopes, language support The Data Fiduciary's own obligations GST / e-invoice GSTIN, HSN, tax lines, IRN Structured tax lines and document references in carts and term sheets Invoice generation and IRP reporting Bhashini and vernacular voice Translation, speech and voice channels Multilingual fields, voice and IVR channels, voice-consent evidence The language models themselves

docs.title: ONDC and Beckn
docs.text:
ONDC is an open network of buyer apps and seller apps built on the Beckn protocol. Beckn defines an asynchronous grammar: each request (search, select, init, confirm, status, cancel, update) gets an acknowledgement and then an on_* callback. Participants are listed in a registry with their public signing keys, and messages are signed with HTTP signatures that the receiver checks against the registry. ONDC adds domain specifications, the Issue and Grievance Management (IGM) flow and specifications for reconciliation and settlement service providers.

What BACP uses. BACP uses Beckn as its transactional backbone. Discovery is Beckn search. A quote is select/on_select. An order is init and confirm. A return is update. A grievance is an IGM issue. BACP does not define a second commerce network.

What BACP adds.

  • A namespaced context.bacp extension that carries the agent identity, presence mode, mandate reference and idempotency key. Participants that do not understand it can ignore it.
  • A gateway inside the buyer app that offers agents a synchronous session with full-state responses over the asynchronous Beckn flow.
  • Mandatory idempotency keys, a replay cache and callbacks bound to the request signature. Beckn treats deduplication as advisory: its message_id "can also be used to ignore duplicate messages". Agents retry often, so BACP makes it mandatory.
  • Agent-raised grievances in IGM, with an evidence bundle attached.
  • Structured negotiation messages that generalise ONDC's per-term status handshake (Assert, Agree, Disagree, Terminate, which ONDC's retail specification uses for payment and settlement terms) to every negotiable term.

What BACP leaves to ONDC. Network participation, onboarding and KYC, catalogue and domain rules, payment terms and settlement between network participants, and network policy all stay with ONDC. BACP does not change the core Beckn messages.

Read more: Beckn / ONDC Binding.

docs.title: UPI
docs.text:
UPI already has the primitives an agent needs to pay without the user present, and these are enforced by NPCI and the issuer, not by the agent.

Primitive What it is How BACP uses it UPI Circle Delegated payments. As of 17-10-2026, NPCI's public page lists limits for IoT and software secondary users of ₹5,000 per transaction, ₹15,000 per month and ₹2,000 in the first 24 hours (the first-24-hours figure is not independently verified), a primary user can add up to five secondary users, and AI and software payments are in a closed-user-group pilot. An open Payment Mandate may bind to a Circle delegation (in.upi.circle, a pilot handler). UPI Reserve Pay A single block, multiple debits (SBMD): the payer blocks funds against a merchant, and the merchant debits them as needed. RBI announced SBMD for UPI in December 2022. NPCI launched Reserve Pay in October 2025 for blocks on credit cards and pre-sanctioned credit lines. As of 17-10-2026, NPCI's Reserve Pay product page and payment-aggregator documentation give at most ₹10,000 per block, reserved for at most 90 days; the payer is notified on each debit and can modify or cancel the reserve before expiry. An open Payment Mandate may bind to a Reserve Pay block (in.upi.reservepay). One block covers one seller. UPI AutoPay Recurring e-mandates. Under RBI's Digital Payments – E-mandate Framework, 2026 (21-04-2026), an additional factor of authentication is needed at registration and for the first debit. Later debits up to ₹15,000 (₹1,00,000 for insurance premiums, mutual fund subscriptions and credit-card bills) need no additional factor, and the issuer sends a pre-debit notice at least 24 hours ahead. An open Payment Mandate may bind to an AutoPay mandate (in.upi.autopay). The agent relays pre-debit notices to the user and never dismisses them. UPI One-Time Mandate A single block for a single later debit, as described in payment-aggregator documentation. BACP has not reviewed an NPCI source for it. An open Payment Mandate may bind to a one-time block (in.upi.otm). Vendor sources disagree on its validity window, so the registry records the conflict. Intent, QR, collect, 123PAY, Lite Payments where the user authenticates each time, or pays from an on-device balance. Usable only with the user present. UPI Lite and UPI Tap & Pay are device-bound and never usable by a remote agent. Refunds and UDIR Refund to the source account. Online dispute resolution and chargebacks. Refunds go back to the original method. Receipts and evidence bundles carry the RRN so that disputes can be joined.

Agent payments on UPI (UAP). Press reports from September 2026 describe an NPCI framework for agent payments on UPI, called the Unified Agent Protocol (reported, not verified as of 17-10-2026). As of 17-10-2026, BACP has found no public NPCI specification or circular for it. BACP therefore reserves a handler slot (in.upi.uap) and does not depend on it. If NPCI publishes such a framework, BACP intends to bind to it in the same way it binds to Circle and Reserve Pay.

Authentication. RBI's Authentication Mechanisms for Digital Payment Transactions Directions, 2025 (issued 25-09-2025) require at least two factors of authentication for digital payments, and, except for card-present transactions, at least one dynamic factor. Compliance was due by 01-04-2026. In BACP the agent is never an authentication factor. A human-present payment uses the user's own UPI PIN, biometric or equivalent on a Trusted Surface. A human-not-present payment runs only under a rail-enforced standing authority that the user set up with full authentication.

What BACP leaves to UPI. Authentication, limits, debit execution, refunds, chargebacks and dispute handling are all NPCI's and the banks'. BACP's payment leg tells the PSP only the payee, the amount, the mandate reference and a hash of the checkout. The rail never sees the basket.

Read more: Rail Bindings and Handler Registry.

docs.title: Other Indian payment rails
docs.text: BACP's handler registry also describes cards (tokens, e-mandates and network agentic tokens), net banking, prepaid wallets and gift cards, NACH, IMPS, NEFT and RTGS, BBPS (Bharat Connect), e-RUPI vouchers, the e₹ (Digital Rupee) pilots, credit at checkout, cash on delivery and bilateral B2B credit (khata). Each is described as data, with its regulator, limits, authentication model, refund route and settlement evidence. Each handler's class says whether it can ever be used without the user present.

docs.title: Account Aggregator and DEPA
docs.text:
The Account Aggregator (AA) framework, built on DEPA, lets a person share financial data through a consent manager that is "data blind": the data passes through it end-to-end encrypted, and RBI's directions do not allow it to keep the data. Its consent artefact is a signed, immutable statement of what may be shared, with whom, for what purpose, how often and until when. Its status is active, paused, revoked or expired, and every use is recorded and notified.

What BACP uses. An agent mandate is very close to an AA consent artefact. BACP mandates borrow its semantics directly: immutable once signed, purpose-coded, use-counted, revocable in part or in full, with notification on every use. The Mandate Manager is modelled on the AA's data-blind consent manager: it stores mandates and logs, never order or payment contents.

What BACP adds. Commerce-specific scopes (buy, pay, cancel, return, raise an issue), periodic budgets, step-up thresholds, and two extra states: exhausted, when the budget is used up, and rejected, when the user declines.

What BACP leaves to AA. BACP does not fetch financial data and does not move money through an AA. Under RBI's directions an AA "shall not support transactions by customers". BACP borrows only the consent model. Where a flow needs financial data, for example for credit at checkout, the AA framework applies as it is.

docs.title: The DPDP Act
docs.text:
The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the DPDP Rules, 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E), published 13-11-2025) govern personal data. Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given with a clear affirmative action. It must come with a notice in clear language, in English or any language in the Eighth Schedule, and it must be as easy to withdraw as to give. The Act provides for Consent Managers registered with the Data Protection Board. Rule 4, which sets out their registration and obligations, applies from 13-11-2026, one year after the Rules were published. Rules 3, 5 to 16, 22 and 23, which hold most other obligations, apply from 13-05-2027, eighteen months after publication, together with most of the Act's duties and its penalties (Act commencement notification G.S.R. 843(E), 13-11-2025).

What BACP adds.

  • A consent receipt for every recipient of the user's data, with the purpose, the data items, the language of the notice and the withdrawal route.
  • Data scopes in each mandate, so that an agent shares only what the purpose needs. A seller gets a delivery address, not a contact list.
  • A Mandate Manager that can register as a DPDP Consent Manager.
  • Pairwise pseudonymous identifiers for users. An Aadhaar number is never used as an identifier.
  • Purchase consent that is never recorded automatically, in line with the e-commerce consumer protection rules.

What BACP leaves to the law. BACP does not decide who is the Data Fiduciary in a given deployment, and it does not replace any party's own DPDP obligations. Open points are listed on the open questions page.

Read more: Mandates and Consent and Security and Privacy.

docs.title: GST and e-invoicing
docs.text:
GST applies to most agent purchases. B2B suppliers above the turnover threshold must register e-invoices with the Invoice Registration Portal (IRP) and obtain an invoice reference number (IRN). Since 01-04-2025, taxpayers with an annual aggregate turnover of ₹10 crore or more cannot report an e-invoice to the IRP more than 30 days after the document date.

What BACP adds. Carts and term sheets carry GST tax lines and HSN codes. For B2B orders the agent passes the buyer's GSTIN and billing details to the seller, and does not alter invoice-relevant data after the IRN is generated. Order state can carry the IRN and the e-way bill number, and documents carry their dates.

What BACP leaves to GST systems. Invoice generation, IRP registration and tax filing remain with the seller and the GST systems.

Read more: Trade Profiles.

docs.title: Bhashini and vernacular voice
docs.text:
Many Indian users will meet an agent by voice, in their own language, and some will use a feature phone. Bhashini, the platform of the National Language Translation Mission under the Ministry of Electronics and IT, provides translation and voice-based language services across Indian languages. UPI 123PAY lets feature-phone users pay without a smartphone, including over IVR, and the user authenticates with the UPI PIN.

What BACP adds.

  • Multilingual text fields as {language: text} maps, so notices, mandate summaries and consent receipts can be shown in the user's language.
  • A channel field covering voice, IVR and 123PAY.
  • Voice-consent evidence: when a confirmation is given by voice, BACP keeps an audio hash, the transcript and the translation, linked to the mandate or order, and logs the model used to translate.
  • A firm rule that voice never replaces the payment's second factor. A voice "yes" can confirm intent. It cannot authenticate a payment.

What BACP leaves to the platforms. BACP does not specify speech or translation models. Bhashini or any equivalent service may be used.

docs.title: What BACP does not decide
docs.text:
Some questions belong to regulators and networks, not to a protocol. BACP keeps them open and makes the evidence complete so that they can be decided:

  • who is liable when an agent makes a mistake within a valid mandate;
  • which body should anchor agent identity for Indian rails;
  • how rail-specific rules, such as pre-debit notice, apply to newer primitives used by agents.

These and other items are tracked on the open questions page. Mapping to specific regulations is on the regulatory mapping page.

docs.title: BACP and other protocols
docs.text:
BACP does not start from scratch. Several open protocols for agentic commerce and agent communication already exist, and BACP reuses their ideas and wire formats wherever they fit. This page explains how BACP relates to each one, and what it takes from each.

The descriptions are based on each protocol's public specification or announcements as of 17-10-2026. These protocols change quickly, so check their own documentation for the current state.

Complementary, not competing

BACP is an India-specific agent layer. It reuses the ideas and, where they fit, the wire formats of the global protocols, so that an agent built for them can work in India with less extra effort, and so that BACP can track their evolution. Where BACP's wire format differs, this page says so.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text: Protocol What it is Mandate or delegation model Indian rails Post-order writes (cancel, return, dispute) Governance BACP Agent layer for Indian commerce over ONDC/Beckn and Indian payment rails Open and closed checkout, payment and negotiation mandates, with periodic budgets, step-up and fast revocation, bound to rail primitives UPI (Circle, Reserve Pay, AutoPay, One-Time Mandate and others), cards, wallets, NACH, BBPS, e-RUPI, COD, B2B credit Yes, through Beckn cancel and update and ONDC IGM Independent open proposal; see GOVERNANCE.md in the repository UCP (Universal Commerce Protocol) Open standard for commerce between platforms, agents and businesses, with capabilities negotiated per business Identity linking with OAuth scopes. Payment authority through an AP2 mandates extension Not covered. Only cards have a normative payment instrument Order retrieval only; an order manage scope is defined, but no write operation Tech Council; founding members include Google and Shopify, and Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Salesforce and Stripe joined on 24-04-2026 (as of 17-10-2026) AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol) Payment-authorisation layer that sits inside a commerce protocol Checkout and payment mandates, open or closed, as SD-JWT credentials; signed receipts Instrument-agnostic; UPI appears only as an example Out of scope; provides dispute evidence Created by Google; donated to the FIDO Alliance, announced 28-04-2026 (as of 17-10-2026) ACP (Agentic Commerce Protocol) Merchant-hosted checkout API for agents, plus delegated payment tokens One-time allowance per checkout session; no standing mandate Not covered. Delegated payment is card-only Order tracking with adjustment status; no write operations Developed by OpenAI and Stripe as an Apache 2.0 open standard (governance body reported, not verified as of 17-10-2026) A2A (Agent2Agent) Protocol for agents to delegate tasks to other agents TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED task state; authorisation left to extensions n/a (transport) n/a Linux Foundation project MCP (Model Context Protocol) Protocol that connects a model host to tools and data OAuth 2.1 scopes, step-up via insufficient_scope; no spend mandate n/a (transport) n/a Agentic AI Foundation, under the Linux Foundation Visa TAP / Intelligent Commerce Network programme for verified agents on card rails Agent-specific tokens, with network controls that match each payment to the user's instruction Card rails only n/a Visa Mastercard Agent Pay / Verifiable Intent Network programme for registered agents on card rails, with an intent credential SD-JWT open and closed mandates (Verifiable Intent) with agentic tokens Card rails only n/a Mastercard; Verifiable Intent (co-developed with Google) was contributed to the FIDO Alliance, announced 28-04-2026 (as of 17-10-2026) x402 HTTP 402 pay-per-request flow None; each request is paid individually Not covered; as of 17-10-2026, implementations settle on blockchain networks n/a x402 Foundation, hosted by the Linux Foundation (announced 02-04-2026; as of 17-10-2026)

docs.title: UCP
docs.text:
The Universal Commerce Protocol is an open standard for interoperable commerce between platforms (such as AI agents), businesses and payment providers. Businesses publish a profile at a well-known URL. Platforms negotiate capabilities such as checkout, cart, catalogue and orders, and the same operations are bound to REST, MCP, A2A and an embedded binding. UCP versions its specification by date.

How BACP relates. BACP's checkout session follows UCP checkout's lifecycle and status names (BACP spells cancelled and adds human_handoff). BACP is not wire-compatible with UCP. Paths, totals and the sign of discounts, the ucp envelope, the complete payload and payment authority, and the MCP argument shape differ. A gateway that lists the capability in.bacp.ucp_checkout also serves a projection in the shape of the UCP checkout, pinned to UCP release v2026-08-25, and UCP clients use that projection. BACP adds what UCP leaves out for India: discovery across a network rather than per business, write paths after an order (cancel, return, grievance), Indian payment rails, DPDP consent and GST.

Where BACP differs from UCP. The table lists every difference that matters to an agent built for UCP, in the order in which such an agent fails. The first row is the one that moves money: a UCP-built agent that reads a BACP discount as a UCP discount shows the buyer an extra charge instead of a saving. UCP facts are as of 18-10-2026, from UCP's release v2026-08-25 (25-08-2026), the latest of its four releases, which is also the release the projection pins (Q-82). Text that UCP added to its main branch after that tag is not in the pinned release and is not described here as UCP's behaviour.

# Difference UCP BACP What a UCP-built agent gets wrong 1 Discount sign A total of type discount or items_discount is a negative integer (exclusiveMaximum: 0) A discount is a non-negative Amount on a Total line of type discount; the total is the sum of the lines Adds the discount to the total: the buyer sees an extra charge, not a saving 2 Declined payment The checkout stays incomplete, with a recoverable payment_failed message The session becomes cancelled, after any earlier tender of a plan has been refunded Offers a retry on a session that has ended 3 canceled against cancelled A platform MUST NOT treat a checkout as canceled unless the business reports status: canceled cancelled (two l's) Never sees a cancelled session as cancelled 4 complete payload and mandate encoding payment is required; an AP2 checkout_mandate is an SD-JWT with key binding Closed Checkout and Payment Mandates as attached compact JWS, with checkout_hash (or a payment_plan) A UCP complete is refused; BACP mandates do not fit UCP's payment 5 continue_url MUST be present on requires_escalation, and the platform escalates through it No continue_url: the step-up carries trusted_surface_url Looks for a URL that is not there, or opens one a business set 6 human_handoff Not in UCP's closed status enum A BACP status, entered by POST /sessions/{session_id}/handoff Cannot parse the status 7 Envelope The checkout carries a required ucp envelope with payment_handlers, and a required links array No envelope; payment handlers are in the gateway's profile Rejects a BACP response as invalid 8 Amount shape A bare integer in minor units {value, currency} A type error on every amount 9 Paths /checkout-sessions, /checkout-sessions/{id}, .../complete, .../cancel /sessions, /sessions/{session_id}, .../complete, .../cancel 404 10 MCP arguments and tool names Tools take id and meta Tools take the request body's properties and the path parameters as flat arguments, and idempotency_key (MCP and A2A) Wrong arguments to a differently named tool 11 Messages content is a string, with a severity content is a LangText language map, with a resolution Cannot read the text or the severity 12 A2A extension header UCP's A2A page activates its extension with X-A2A-Extensions BACP follows A2A 1.0, which names the header A2A-Extensions The extension is not activated

How the two are organised. UCP is organised as services (verticals such as shopping), capabilities inside each service, a common layer shared by all, and extensions that add to a capability. BACP has the same four ideas under different names, and they do not line up one to one. BACP's counterpart of a UCP vertical is a trade profile: a set of rules for one kind of buying (for example B2B trade or public procurement) over the same capabilities. What UCP calls "Common" is spread over BACP's shared artefacts, which every capability uses.

UCP BACP counterpart Where Services and verticals Trade profiles over the same five capabilities Trade Profiles "Common": shared types common.json (for example Amount, integer paise) common.json "Common": errors The flat error object and the error registry Errors "Common": identity of the caller AgentCredential and RFC 9421 signature tags Identity and Request Signing "Common": payment authority Open and closed mandates Mandates and Consent "Common": audit trail Instruction log and evidence bundle Evidence and Instruction Log Capabilities (checkout, order, catalogue) in.bacp.discover, in.bacp.checkout, in.bacp.mandate, in.bacp.order, in.bacp.issue Discovery Extensions The extensibility rules: ignore unknown fields (but refuse a member of an unlisted capability with capability_unsupported), fail closed on unknown mandate constraints, namespaced extensions, registered error codes and handlers; third-party capabilities only through capability_declarations and a digest-pinned registry, with the payload under ext.<id> and no schema fetched at run time Extensibility, Capability declarations

Among the UCP parts with no BACP counterpart in this version are the cart capability, linking a buyer's account at a seller, ask (natural-language questions to a business, which is on UCP's main branch after v2026-08-25 and in no release as of 18-10-2026), permalink (a browser-addressable intent), location search and lookup, and a second vertical, lodging. These are parked, not rejected, each with the controls it needs written into an open question: the cart (Q-95), linking a buyer's account at a seller (Q-96), ask (Q-97), loyalty (Q-98), catalogue lookup by id and variants (Q-99) and purchasable ranking parameters (Q-100). The UCP projection answers 404 for them. A third party can define a new capability only through capability_declarations and the digest-pinned registry, which activates once a registry review exists (Q-94); how a new vertical is added stays an open topic.

What BACP does not take from UCP. BACP does not adopt UCP's Embedded Protocol, in which a business's own checkout page runs inside the platform's surface and can collect payment and address details. This is a non-goal, not a gap. In BACP the principal's authorisation happens on the Trusted Surface, the non-agentic surface of the Mandate Manager or the payer's PSP, which renders only gateway-signed content in the principal's language and takes the PIN or biometric itself. A seller's page does not take part: it is not non-agentic by requirement, it cannot be checked against a signed render, and putting a PIN or a consent on a seller's page would put the factor within reach of the party that benefits from the answer. A merchant-supplied view for a human to review a basket before approving stays parked; if it is added, the approval would still be given on the Trusted Surface.

What BACP reuses from UCP.

  • Checkout session lifecycle and status names, and recovery when a response is lost.
  • The pattern of defining operations once and binding them to REST, MCP and A2A.
  • HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421) with Content-Digest (RFC 9530), with ES256 and EdDSA (Ed25519) both mandatory to verify.
  • Idempotency-Key semantics and date-based versioning.
  • Capability intersection between the two parties' profiles, and payment handlers as a concept.
  • The approach to publishing the specification: MkDocs with an unversioned landing site and versioned specification paths.

docs.title: AP2
docs.text:
The Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) is a security layer for agent payments that sits inside a commerce protocol. As of 17-10-2026, version 0.2 (released in April 2026) defines checkout and payment mandates, each open (constraints) or closed (exact cart or payment), as SD-JWT credentials with key binding. A non-agentic Trusted Surface collects the user's consent, and each verifier returns a signed receipt. AP2 assumes that agents may be attackers and requires verification in deterministic code. On 28-04-2026 the FIDO Alliance announced that Google had donated AP2 to it, and work on the specification continues in FIDO working groups (as of 17-10-2026).

How BACP relates. BACP's mandate model is AP2 v0.2's model, with Indian semantics added. BACP adds periodic budgets (AP2's budget is cumulative over the mandate's life), category and PIN code allow-lists, step-up thresholds, cancel, return and grievance scopes, revocation with a short propagation target, and a PSP-attested binding to a live UPI primitive. Negotiation bounds are carried in a separate negotiation mandate, so that AP2 verifiers, which fail closed on unknown constraints, still accept BACP's Checkout and Payment Mandates.

What BACP reuses from AP2.

  • Open and closed Checkout and Payment Mandates, encoded as SD-JWT with key binding to the agent's key.
  • The non-agentic Trusted Surface for consent and authentication.
  • Fail-closed evaluation of constraints, and treating the agent as untrusted.
  • Signed receipts from each verifier, as the basis of dispute evidence.

docs.title: ACP
docs.text:
The Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP) defines a merchant-hosted REST API for checkout sessions, in which the merchant remains the system of record, and a delegated payment API that issues a vault token limited by an allowance. OpenAI and Stripe developed ACP and were its first implementers. ACP was described as being in beta (reported, not verified as of 17-10-2026).

How BACP relates. ACP's allowance is single-use and tied to one checkout session, and its delegated payment is card-only. BACP needs standing mandates for when the user is not present, and Indian rails. BACP borrows ACP's response and error conventions, which are well suited to agents.

What BACP reuses from ACP.

  • Authoritative full-state responses on every call.
  • The flat error object and messages[] with a resolution hint.
  • Strict idempotency rules: a missing key, a conflicting body, a request still in flight and a replay each have a defined response.

docs.title: A2A and MCP
docs.text:
A2A lets agents delegate tasks to other agents. MCP connects a model host to tools and data. Neither defines commerce or payments. They are transports.

How BACP relates. BACP is bound to both, as UCP is. A BACP gateway can be offered as MCP tools and as an A2A extension, as well as over REST.

What BACP reuses.

  • From A2A: the agent card for discovery, the TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED task state as the point where a step-up is requested, and structured data parts for BACP objects.
  • From MCP: tool bindings with structured content, OAuth 2.1 with audience-bound tokens, and the insufficient_scope challenge as the step-up trigger.

Read more: MCP and A2A.

docs.title: Visa Trusted Agent Protocol and Mastercard Agent Pay
docs.text:
Card networks run their own agent programmes. Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol signs agent requests with RFC 9421, using different signature tags for browsing and for paying (agent-browser-auth and agent-payer-auth in its reference code), with created and expires timestamps and a nonce. Visa Intelligent Commerce issues agent-specific payment tokens and checks each payment against the user's authenticated instruction. In Mastercard Agent Pay only registered agents can transact, using Mastercard network tokens. Verifiable Intent, which Mastercard published as an open specification, contributed to the FIDO Alliance (announced 28-04-2026) and plans to integrate into Agent Pay (as of 17-10-2026), is a layered SD-JWT credential that carries the user's Checkout and Payment Mandates.

How BACP relates. These programmes cover card rails. BACP covers the Indian rails around them, and can carry a network agentic token as one payment handler among many.

What BACP reuses.

  • Separate signature tags for browsing and paying, which BACP extends with tags for post-order actions, negotiation and the Trusted Surface.
  • Nonce-bound, short-lived signatures with a replay cache.
  • A handler for network agentic tokens (in.card.agentic), marked as a pilot.

docs.title: x402
docs.text:
x402 is an HTTP 402 flow for paying per request: the server answers with a payment challenge, the client retries with a signed payment, and a facilitator verifies and settles it. As of 17-10-2026, implementations settle in stablecoins and tokens on blockchain networks. The specification says it aims to support fiat networks too.

How BACP relates. x402 addresses per-request payment for APIs and content, not the order lifecycle. It does not cover INR rails. BACP does not use x402 today. The 402 challenge pattern may be worth reusing for paid APIs on Indian rails in the future.

docs.title: Summary of reuse
docs.text: From BACP reuses UCP Checkout lifecycle and status names (not wire-compatible), REST, MCP and A2A transport bindings (UCP has a fourth, embedded binding, which BACP does not adopt), RFC 9421 and RFC 9530 signing, idempotency keys, date-based versions, capability intersection AP2 Open and closed mandates as SD-JWT with key binding, the non-agentic Trusted Surface, fail-closed constraints, signed receipts ACP Full-state responses, flat errors with resolution hints, strict idempotency responses A2A Agent card, TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED step-up, data parts MCP Tool binding, OAuth 2.1 audience-bound tokens, insufficient_scope step-up Visa TAP, Mastercard Agent Pay Browse and pay signature tags, nonce-bound signatures, agentic tokens as a handler ONDC / Beckn The transaction grammar, registry, post-order flows and IGM (see BACP and India's DPI) Account Aggregator Consent-artefact semantics for mandates (see BACP and India's DPI)

docs.title: Status: version 2026-10-18
docs.text:
BACP 2026-10-18 is the first dated release of the specification. Implementers can target it.

  • The release is published at /2026-10-18/ and aliased as /latest/. Work towards later releases continues on the main branch, published as draft. See Versioning.
  • The schemas, the OpenAPI binding and the payment-handler registry validate, and the examples are checked against them on every change.
  • Some rules depend on owner decisions that are still pending. These rules are marked Proposed in the specification, link to the open questions, and may change in a later dated release.
  • The conformance test suite is not yet published, so no participant can hold a conformance attestation yet.
  • BACP is an independent open proposal. As of 17-10-2026, no production deployments have been announced, and no public body has endorsed it.

This roadmap describes intent. It is not a commitment to deliver specific features by specific dates, and it will change with review feedback. Dates are given only once they can be justified.

docs.title: 1. Owner decisions and open questions
docs.text:
Several questions are still open after the first dated release, and rules that depend on them are marked Proposed. Some are design choices the maintainers can make. Others depend on regulators, networks or rail operators. Examples include:

  • how liability for an agent's error within a valid mandate should be allocated, and what evidence each party needs;
  • which body should anchor agent identity on Indian rails;
  • how rail rules such as pre-debit notice apply to newer primitives used by agents;
  • conflicting public limits for some payment primitives, which the handler registry records rather than resolves.

The full list, with the current proposal for each, is on the open questions page. Rules that depend on them stay marked Proposed until they are decided.

docs.title: 2. Later dated releases
docs.text: BACP versions its specification by date (YYYY-MM-DD). The first dated release, 2026-10-18, is published at /2026-10-18/ and aliased as /latest/. Later dated releases will be cut from main as open questions are decided, and will follow the deprecation and breaking-change notice rules in Versioning.

docs.title: 3. Reference implementation and SDKs
docs.text:
An open-source reference implementation of the BACP gateway is planned, covering:

  • the session facade over Beckn, with idempotency and replay protection;
  • the deterministic mandate verifier and the negotiation guard;
  • the instruction log and evidence bundles;
  • bindings for REST, MCP and A2A.

Client SDKs for agent builders, and helpers for sellers and PSPs, are planned to follow.

docs.title: 4. Conformance suite
docs.text: BACP treats conformance as data. A conformance suite will provide test cases, expected outcomes and invariants checked after every case, organised by conformance level, so that an implementation can show what it supports. See Conformance.

docs.title: 5. Sandbox
docs.text: A public sandbox is planned, with simulated sellers, a simulated Mandate Manager and simulated payment rails, so that agent builders can try the full lifecycle (discovery, checkout, negotiation, payment, return and grievance) without touching real money or a production network.

docs.title: 6. Stakeholder review
docs.text: BACP's maintainers intend to seek review from NPCI, ONDC, RBI-regulated entities such as banks and payment aggregators, network participants, consumer groups and data-protection practitioners. This describes BACP's intent only. It does not imply that any of these bodies has agreed to review, support or adopt BACP.

docs.title: Get involved
docs.text: Review the specification, comment on the open questions, and open issues or pull requests on GitHub. See CONTRIBUTING.md in the repository for how to contribute.
